claims.text: A high-entropy alloy with an optimized composition can be used to prepare parts for hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
Such a high-entropy alloy can protect dipping and plating equipment from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
AlCoCrFeNi is a candidate high-entropy alloy for this application.
The relevant liquid-aluminum immersion temperature is around 700°C.
A protective oxide layer forms on the high-entropy alloy during exposure.
Alloying elements in the high-entropy alloy react with environmental oxygen.
The reaction with oxygen produces a stable oxide layer.
The oxide layer prevents penetration of liquid aluminum.
Preventing liquid-aluminum penetration reduces corrosion of the high-entropy alloy.
The high-entropy alloy will reduce corrosion rate by at least 50% relative to conventional materials used in hot-dip aluminum plating.
Steel and aluminum alloys are examples of conventional materials used in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
The high-entropy alloy must withstand temperatures up to 800°C.
The high-entropy alloy must maintain its corrosion resistance at temperatures up to 800°C.
The exact high-entropy-alloy composition and optimal processing conditions remain unknown.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 50% corrosion-rate reduction, whereas the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only below 30%. A result between 30% and 49% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
